thread:
mike: Quick heads-up — nightly perf run showed a spike in p50 after the kernel-hint change. profile uploaded to perf-bucket.

sophia: saw it too. p50 up ~45ms on a handful of nodes. which run?

mike: run 2026-03-17T03:12Z. nodes 7/9. I attached the calling graph and kernel-selection trace.

perf-bot: [perf-run] 2026-03-17T03:12Z results uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/runs/3959998888

ryan: early hypothesis: continuous batcher is forming more microbatches post-hint. kernel selection now prefers wave-kernel at shorter seq -> less coalescing -> higher latency.

anya: did KV cache hit rates change? fewer prefetched tokens will hurt decode path.

mike: KV hit dropped from 0.78 -> 0.62 on the impacted nodes during spike window.

dmitri: that's a big drop. Could be admit policy starving prefetch. What are token_budget targets right now?

sophia: live config: token_budget=128, burst=256, admit_soft_limit=0.85. kernel_hint flip went out last night.

ryan: propose canary rollback of kernel_hint in one pool to confirm. also try increasing token_budget to 256 to allow larger batches.

anya: also think queue-admit needs to allow more prefetch tokens queued. our soft-429 currently rejects earlier which may prevent batch assembly.

elaine: I can run a focused replay with kvcache traces + new kernel config. want A/B.

mike: run two configs: A) kernel_hint=off; token_budget=128 (baseline). B) kernel_hint=on; token_budget=256; admit_soft_limit=0.9

perf-bot: job queued: perf/replays/3959998888-A and perf/replays/3959998888-B

sophia: note: batching window is 8ms. if kernel picks wave-kernel expecting longer seqs, early-assembly rules reduce coalescing.

dmitri: idea: adjust batch-assembly to wait longer when kvcache hit rate is low. e.g. wait_ms=12 when kv_hit<0.7.

ryan: quick patch to test: continuous_batcher: { max_wait_ms: 12, min_coalesce_tokens: 32 }

anya: also consider a soft-requeue instead of hard 429 for some fraction: requeue to low-priority lane so prefetch can rebuild KV cache.

sophia: API semantics are tricky. maybe 429 with Retry-After is safer externally; internal lane requeues ok for canary/test.

mike: for canary, let's set soft 429 threshold to 0.95 and run probabilistic requeue (10%) to observe behavior.

elaine: launching replays now. ETA ~20m.

perf-bot: replay finished. A (baseline) p50=210ms, B (token_budget=256) p50=172ms. KV hit improved to 0.75 on B.

anya: nice delta ~38ms. what's p95?

perf-bot: p95 A=420ms, B=405ms (small improvement). tail variance reduced slightly.

sophia: promising. suggests larger token budgets let batcher coalesce more despite kernel hint.

ryan: add telemetry: per-batch kernel_choice, batch_size, kv_hit_rate to traces for correlation.

mike: agree. If this holds in canary we should: 1) keep kernel_hint on, 2) raise default token_budget for affected model family, 3) relax admit_soft_limit to 0.9.

dmitri: also update batcher docs about kernel-selection -> batching interactions.

elaine: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/+/1234 — includes config diff and canary playbook. will run canary rollout after merge :rocket:

sophia: :thumbsup: please attach the load profiles and kvcache traces used to the PR.

mike: I'll open follow-up to implement ryan's tracing fields and dmitri's adaptive wait-ms patch.

anya: long-term we should consider an admit policy that is kvcache-aware: if kv_hit low, bias admit to build larger coalesced batches rather than early 429.

ryan: agreed. maybe a score: admit_score = alpha * kv_hit + beta * queue_depth + gamma * kernel_latency_hint

elaine: logging note: add a dashboard showing kv_hit vs p50 over last 7d so we can detect regressions sooner.

perf-bot: canary rollout metrics (1h): p50 down 15ms on canary pool, kv_hit +0.06, error rate unchanged.

mike: closing actions: PR merge + canary rollout (elaine), tracing fields PR (ryan), doc update (dmitri), follow-up sync tomorrow 10:00am PT.

sophia: thanks all.

mike: thanks. we'll monitor closely and revert if anything regresses.
